description.narrative: Towards sustainable access to justice for legal empowerment in the Kyrgyz Republic. description.narrative: 1.1 Established and operational FLA coordination center 1.2 Introduced and operational mechanisms for provision of legal aid on civil and administrative cases 1.3 FLA quality standards adopted and integrated into the work of Ministry of Justice (MoJ) FLA center 1.4 Free legal consultations provided through MoJ FLA centers and Bus of Solidarity (disaggregated by gender and PwDs) 1.5 Coordination platforms and regional\global cooperation established 2.1 Strengthened capacity of civil society organizations to empower women and PwDs in the fulfilment of their rights, as well as monitoring the progress 2.2 Media strategy with particular focus on women and PwDs’ rights developed and implemented

comment.narrative: 1.1 New Free Legal Aid (FLA) law adopted. FLA coordination center is not established yet. 1.2 New FLA law includes civil and administrative cases. No mechanisms for provision of legal aid on civil and administrative cases. 1.3 Quality standards for criminal cases developed and for civil and administrative cases are being developed 1.4 7 200 people (4122 women and 3078 men) received free legal consultations 1.5 No regular meetings of the coordination platform 2.1 4 developed training modules on the rights of: 1) women; 2) children; 3) people with disabilities (PwDs); 4) youth integrated into the training programmes of 4 state bodies training centers 2.2 No targeted media strategy. 4 developed training modules on the rights of: 1) women; 2) children; 3) PwDs; 4) youth integrated into the training programmes of 4 state bodies training centers 2.3 UN CRPD is signed, but not ratified

1.1 Trained Ministry of Justices (MoJ) Free legal aid coordination center (FLACC)employees (men and women) 1.2 Implementation of the action plan on integrating civil and administrative cases started 1.3 FLA quality standards integration into the work of MoJ FLACC started 1.4 6000 people received free legal consultations 1.5 Coordination meetings conducted at least twice a year 2.1. Selected components of the media strategy implemented by at least 8 Women and people with disabilities (PwDs) rights protection CSOs in the selected provinces covering 8 districts and Bishkek and Osh cities 2.2. 1.1 An online training on development of effective communication skills has been conducted on 13-15 May, for 18 FLA Coordination Center’s staff, including 7 women and 11 men. 1.2 The Action Plan for the introduction of qualified legal aid in civil and administrative cases is currently under implementation. 1.3 Free legal aid quality standards are integrated into the Free Legal Aid Coordination Centers work 1.4 More than 6,000 people received free legal consultations 1.5 Two coordination meetings conducted: one with civil society organizations, legal clinics and the other with state bodies 2.1 Two civil society organizations consortiums started implementation of the grant projects on elimination of stereotypes towards rural women and people with disabilities and their rights 2.2.Wide media campaign conducted in accordance with the strategy. On-line training module for journalists on coverage of the people with disabilities issues developed and to be introduced into the local universities plans in January 2021 2.3 59 sign-language interpreters trained on legal specifics. Web-sites of the Ministry of Justice and Ministry of Labor and Social Development became accessible for people with visual disabilities. Regulation on provision of sign-language interpretation is to be signed by the Prime Minister and funds allocated. Media campaign conducted devoted to the International Day of persons with disabilities

1.1 Budget of the Ministry of Justices Free Legal Aid center developed and approved 1.2 Implementation of the action plan on integrating civil and administrative cases in process 1.3 Trained attorneys on the standards for provision of free legal aid 1.4 6000 people received free legal consultations 1.5 Coordination meetings conducted at least twice a year 2.1. Increased number of targeted applicants for free legal aid and services provided as a result of the interventions of women and people with disabilities rights protection civil society organizations 2.2. Conducted media campaign in accordance with the strategy. Introduced training on coverage of PwDs and women’s’ rights into the country’s leading mass media 2.3. Implemented activities of UN CRPD Action Plan (selected) related to the project

1.1 Ministry of Justice Free Legal Aid centers budget is developed and approved with the total amount of about 77 114.2 thousand soms. 1.2 New Free Legal Aid law including mechanisms for provision of free legal aid in civil and administrative cases adopted by the Parliament on 20 October 2021. 1.3 Training for the attorneys on the standards for provision of FLA conducted. A total of 260 lawyers (out of 320) from the state free legal aid registry, including 184 men and 76 women took part in the training. 1.4 More than 6000 people received free legal consultations 1.5 Two coordination meetings conducted in 2021 2.1 According to the introduced accounting of tear-off coupons within the framework of the Rural Women project, the number of applications to the FLA Centers and Bus of Solidarity amounted to 2125 people: 925 in Osh region, and 1200 in Chui region, which is an average of 21% of the total number of applications to the FLA Centers in Chui and Osh regions.;8. In the course of 30 trainings, the number of PwDs applying to the FLA Centers and the Bus of Solidarity significantly increased. According to data obtained from the Coordination Councils of 15 districts, the number of appeals increased by 200% on average in each district. 2.2Cooperation with four universities of the country was established on introduction of training module into the training programs of the faculties of journalism of the Kyrgyz State University, Osh State University, Ala-Too International University, as well as the Department of Journalism at the International University of Kyrgyzstan. 13 media outlets signed a memorandum on the coverage of disability issues based on the UN CRPD principles: Channel 7, ElTR, Azattyk, Osh Pirim TV Channel, Birinchi Radio, Radio Sanzhira, Radio Maral FM, Super Info, Batken Media Center, Naryn Media Center, Newspaper Szaman Kyrgyzstan , Media PolitClinika , and Den Sooluk Magazine. 2.3 Expert analysis of current legislative acts, state programmes and strategies as well as other resolutions made by the Kyrgyz Government to determine their compliance with or contradiction to the UNCRPD and to reveal any legislative provisions discriminatory to persons with disabilities conducted and results presented to the key stakeholders.
The Project is aimed to be completed in March 2022, the project evaluation is supposed to be finalized.
To be reported at the end of 2022
